messages.subject: chi-square for a bivariate regression
parts:

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: chi-square for a bivariate regression
parts:
On 02/04/2013 06:37 PM, Tom Kraft wrote:
> Hi,
>
> For the purpose of model comparison, I am running a simple bivariate
> regression in lavaan along with several other more complex models. The
> problem I face is that the lavaan output gives me a chi-square value of
> 0 (with 0 df) for the simple regression model.
>

> Could you please help me understand why I am not able to get a
> chi-square value for my model

Your model is saturated. It has as many (free) parameters as data points
(= elements in the covariance matrix). All regression models are
saturated (unless you impose specific restrictions).

But that is not a problem. You can still use the AICc value, but you
need to use the formula using the logl (not the chi-square value).

Yves.

parts:
Hi Yves,

Thank you for reply (and your excellent package!). I understand now why saturation of my model is causing the output for the chi-square. However, you mention that I can remedy this by using the loglikelihood to calculate AICc. This was indeed what I tried first, but I have run into problems with the way lavaan is calculating logL and AIC for path analysis.

I began looking into this when comparing models with AIC from lavaan. In particular, and contrary to what I would expect, models in my set with highly significant and powerful predictors are associated with higher AIC values than models with seemingly unrelated variables. As such, I'm not certain whether the AIC reported by lavaan can be used to compare among models. It seems as though the likelihoods generated are perhaps meant to assess the fit of a particular path model rather than being useful for comparison to other models.

Could you please help clarify what the AIC from lavaan is reporting? And if I am not correct above, do you understand why I am getting the counter-intuitive results described? 

Thank you again,
Tom

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: chi-square for a bivariate regression
parts:
> I began looking into this when comparing models with AIC from lavaan. In
> particular, and contrary to what I would expect, models in my set with
> highly significant and powerful predictors are associated with higher
> AIC values than models with seemingly unrelated variables.

Currently, the (log)likelihood computed by lavaan is using ALL
variables. Including the exogenous variables (even if fixed.x=TRUE). Not
only the dependent variables, as you perhaps expect when fitting
regression models only.

This is the typical 'SEM' approach, where modeling the covariance matrix
is the prime objective. Not prediction.

Yves.
